summary: Tested the new escalation/panic/evidence/photo feature batch on top of the Digital Mate security MVP. Backend: 24/24 pytest tests pass — 7 brand new tests cover trap escalation L1->L2->L3 (with L3 auto-lock + lost_mode + owner_alert + critical access_attempt events), owner-score resets streak, POST /api/security/evidence/photo + GET /api/security/events round-trip with metadata.photo preserved, POST /api/security/panic (locks device + lost_mode true + trap_active false + last_location stored + owner alert created), GET /api/security/alerts shape (alerts/count/unread). Also updated the previous iteration_1 scoring tests to match the new escalation semantics (L1 first hit is warning + trap_active=false, L2 second hit goes critical + trap_active=true) — both pass now. Frontend (mobile 390x844, via 'Try the Demo →'): panic-btn opens panic-confirm-modal, panic-confirm-btn triggers /panic (backend confirmed locked=true, lost_mode=true, trap_level=3, alert created), navigates to Recovery tab, and dashboard then shows 'Lost Phone mode active'. Evidence Center renders seeded intruder photos as data-testid='evidence-photo' thumbnails, click opens evidence-lightbox, LEVEL badges display on escalation events. Owner Recognition: ONE click of 'Capture my behaviour' now trains the model (sample_count 9, trained=true after a single click, as required).

issues: The Emergent badge still overlaps the fixed bottom-nav on 390x844 (had to JS-hide it during tests). Pre-existing issue from iteration_1, not a regression.

action_items: (Optional UX) Ensure bottom-nav z-index sits above the Emergent badge on mobile so users are never blocked tapping nav items — still pending from iteration_1.

(Optional polish) The headless test browser blocks getUserMedia, so capturePhoto inserts a 'Camera capture blocked' event with no metadata.photo — works as designed but worth documenting in user-facing docs.
critical_code_review_comments: security_engine.py /score escalation is correct and deterministic: streak tracked in device_state, L3 sets locked=true + lost_mode=true + creates owner_alert. Only logs an event when escalating to a HIGHER level (no spam). Good.
/panic correctly sets trap_active=false at L3 (the device is locked by owner, not in decoy), stores last_location + push to location_history (capped at 50), and creates an alert. Good.
/evidence/photo stores the data URL inside metadata.photo of an intruder_photo critical event — clean reuse of the events store, surfaced by EvidenceCenter as a thumbnail.

FEATURE_KEYS, MIN_SAMPLES_TO_TRAIN=8 and OWNER_TRUST_THRESHOLD=0.60 are sensible defaults. OwnerRecognition now sends 8 samples in one click (fixes iteration_1 feedback) — single tap reaches the trained state.
/recovery/wipe still requires owner_code + confirm=true (403/400 guards intact). /trap/deactivate still requires owner_code (403 guard intact). No regression.
EvidenceCenter location row uses openstreetmap.org maps link (not google maps) — clickable <a> with href to /?mlat=&mlon=#map=16/.. — works.
App.js guard loop captures photo at L2 and sendAlert at L3 once per episode (capturedRef/notifiedRef), starts GPS tracking every 120s, resets refs when level back to 0. Clean.
No mongo _id leakage observed in any response.

success_rate.frontend: 100% (panic + evidence photo + lightbox + LEVEL badges + one-click training all verified)

context_for_next_testing_agent: To test FE photo rendering, seed via POST /api/security/evidence/photo using the SAME device_id the browser uses (set localStorage 'dm_device_id' BEFORE reload). Use mobile viewport 390x844 and click 'Try the Demo →'. Hide #emergent-badge via JS before tapping bottom-nav (data-testid='nav-evidence' / 'nav-recovery' / 'nav-home' / 'nav-mate'). Map links use openstreetmap.org (NOT google.com/maps). getUserMedia + geolocation are blocked headless — capturePhoto logs a placeholder 'Camera capture blocked' event with no photo data; for thumbnail rendering tests, ALWAYS seed via API.
rca of the issue: N/A — no functional bugs found. All new escalation, panic, evidence-photo, alerts, and one-click training behaviours work end-to-end.
